settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: The factory is configured with an application schema (aegis.xsd) via setSchema, which may reject documents containing DTDs or non-conforming content.
The schema resource is loaded from a fixed absolute classpath path (/META-INF/cxf/aegis.xsd), not from external input.
Elsewhere in the project StaxUtils explicitly sets XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD=false and IS_REPLACING_ENTITY_REFERENCES=false, showing awareness of XML abuse and suggesting other paths are hardened.
I did not observe runtime-controlled input reaching the descriptor parse path in the reviewed lines.
candidates.description: In rt/databinding/aegis/src/main/java/org/apache/cxf/aegis/type/XMLTypeCreator.java a static DocumentBuilderFactory (AEGIS_DOCUMENT_BUILDER_FACTORY) is created at class init and configured only with setNamespaceAware(true) and an optional XSD schema from the fixed classpath resource /META-INF/cxf/aegis.xsd. I did not find any code in this class that disables DTD support, external general/parameter entities, or the loading of external DTDs/Schemas (e.g., via disallow-doctype-decl, external-general-entities=false, or accessExternalDTD). The class also caches parsed Documents keyed by class name. If the .aegis.xml descriptor content is ever attacker-influenced (parsed through a builder derived from this factory), classic XML parser abuse such as XXE (local/remote file or SSRF disclosure) or entity-expansion DoS would be plausible. This is flagged as a candidate only; the exact result of createDocumentBuilder() and how descriptor InputStreams are acquired was not fully traced, and the schema-based validation path may constrain accepted documents.
missing_evidence: The implementation of the method that invokes createDocumentBuilder()/parse() with descriptor input, and where its InputStream originates (classpath resource vs. remote/attacker-controlled).
Whether JAXP parsing of the aegis schema-validated document actually permits external entity resolution.
Any global JAXP hardening (system properties such as javax.xml.accessExternalDTD) applied in the deployment.
Confirmation that no external entity/schema document can be dereferenced under the schema-validated configuration.
preconditions: Attacker can influence the content and/or source location of an Aegis XML descriptor (.aegis.xml) processed by XMLTypeCreator.
The underlying JAXP DocumentBuilderFactory/parser does not enforce DTD/entity restrictions by default in the runtime environment.
candidates.title: Aegis XMLTypeCreator DocumentBuilderFactory lacks explicit DTD/external-entity hardening when parsing descriptor XML
